metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (against the checkout-gerrit-change-action source/docs, not training knowledge) the exact Gerrit-direct fetch URL form the fix's step-2 fallback must reproduce — including project path, any '.git' suffix, and auth — and cite that evidence in the plan, or fetch the refspec only from the actions/checkout origin remote and treat an un-replicated ref as an explicit fetch failure.
evidence: Plan: 'falls back to anonymous HTTPS https://${{ vars.GERRIT_SERVER }}/${{ inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT }}, matching the checkout action's existing Gerrit fallback surface'
gerrit-verify.yaml:75 and jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml:62 pass only 'gerrit-url: https://${{ vars.GERRIT_SERVER }}' (no /<project> path)

docs/adr/0021-replication-change-refs.md:27-31 states the action 'falls back to fetching directly from the Gerrit server (gerrit-url)' but does not establish the /<GERRIT_PROJECT> path or anonymous-HTTPS form
The specific fallback URL path is a claim about the third-party action's internal URL construction not settleable from repo files
findings.finding: Step 2's fallback fetch premise — that anonymous HTTPS 'https://${{ vars.GERRIT_SERVER }}/${{ inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT }}' matches 'the checkout action's existing Gerrit fallback surface' — is unverified against the repo; every checkout-gerrit-change-action call site supplies only 'gerrit-url: https://${{ vars.GERRIT_SERVER }}' with no project path, and ADR-0021 documents only a generic 'gerrit-url' fallback, never the /<project> URL form.
scenarios: Replication lag: the patchset ref has not reached the GitHub mirror, so step 2 must use the Gerrit fallback fetch — if the constructed URL path is wrong (e.g. Gerrit needs '/a/<project>', a '.git' suffix, or auth), the fallback fetch fails and the fix cannot validate the refspec

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit temporary-git test (or extend the named one) that exercises the unfetchable-refspec path so AC2's 'cannot be fetched ... fails with a clear fetch/input error' claim has a proving command distinct from the mismatch-pair test.
evidence: AC2: 'If the requested patchset refspec cannot be fetched from either the GitHub mirror or Gerrit fallback, the workflow fails with a clear fetch/input error'

Fix plan describes only: 'its validation shell must fail on an inconsistent temporary-git refspec/revision pair without checking out the refspec commit' — this is the mismatch case, not the fetch-failure case
The two are distinct branches: fetch-fails (network/ref missing) vs fetch-succeeds-but-SHA-differs
findings.finding: AC2 names a failure mode (refspec 'cannot be fetched from either the GitHub mirror or Gerrit fallback') but the described test coverage in the fix plan only exercises the inconsistent refspec/revision pair (a successful fetch that mismatches), not an unfetchable-refspec path; the proving command may pass without ever exercising the fetch-failure branch AC2 claims.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC2 / Fix plan steps 2-3 / test strengthening paragraph
scenarios: A dispatch supplies a refspec that no longer exists on the mirror or Gerrit; the fetch itself errors and the intended clear fetch/input error must fire
findings.suggested_fix: In the test-strengthening paragraph, name two contract tests: (1) mismatched-but-fetchable refspec/revision pair fails without checkout; (2) unfetchable refspec (both origin and Gerrit HTTPS fallback fail) surfaces a clear fetch error and leaves HEAD at GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the authoritative checkout to GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION preserves ADR-0021's mirror-first-then-Gerrit-server fallback (e.g. fetch refs first with the fallback surface, THEN check out the revision) so a not-yet-replicated patchset does not hard-fail before any Gerrit fallback runs.
evidence: docs/adr/0021-replication-change-refs.md: 'Replication lag is tolerated by a fallback, not a hard dependency. checkout-gerrit-change-action fetches GERRIT_REFSPEC from the GitHub mirror first and falls back to fetching directly from the Gerrit server ... if the ref hasn't replicated yet.'
Plan step 1: 'Use the already-approved, SHA-pinned actions/checkout action to check out ref: ${{ inputs.GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION }}'
Plan step 2 (the fallback-bearing fetch) is ordered AFTER step 1's authoritative checkout: 'Run a shell validation step that fetches GERRIT_REFSPEC ... falls back to anonymous HTTPS ...'
actions/checkout's only configured remote is the GitHub mirror (origin); it has no Gerrit fallback.
findings.finding: The fix's authoritative checkout (step 1, actions/checkout with ref: GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION) discards the Gerrit-server fallback that ADR-0021 relies on to tolerate replication lag; under lag the patchset SHA may be absent from the GitHub mirror (origin), so step 1 fails before step 2's fallback fetch ever runs.
scenarios: A patchset is dispatched for parity before Gerrit→GitHub replication of its refs/changes/* ref completes (the lag window ADR-0021 exists to absorb): step 1's actions/checkout cannot find the SHA on the mirror and fails, even though a Gerrit fetch would succeed.
findings.suggested_fix: Reorder so the fallback-bearing fetch of the patchset (mirror-first, Gerrit HTTPS fallback) happens BEFORE the working-tree lands on the revision, then `git checkout <GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION>` from the fetched objects; or keep checkout-gerrit-change-action and add a follow-up `git checkout` of the revision.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider the step ordering so the refspec fetch (with mirror + anonymous-HTTPS fallback) is the mechanism that lands the working tree on the patchset, with the SHA equality check as the guard — rather than making the refspec fetch a validator that only runs after an unverified SHA-first checkout succeeds.
evidence: Plan sequences checkout (step 1) strictly before the refspec fetch (step 2); if step 1 aborts on an unresolvable SHA, step 2 never executes
The authoritative requested commit per the plan is GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION, yet the plan uses the refspec fetch only as a post-hoc validator, not as the checkout mechanism
findings.finding: Step 2's fallback fetch presupposes a successful step-1 checkout ('fetches from the existing `origin` remote created by `actions/checkout`'), so the refspec fetch/fallback that is meant to be the authoritative resolver only runs AFTER the unverified SHA checkout has already succeeded — the ordering makes the fallback unable to rescue the failure mode in step 1.
findings.location: Fix plan step 2 ("fetches `GERRIT_REFSPEC` into `FETCH_HEAD` … from the existing `origin` remote created by `actions/checkout` … falls back to anonymous HTTPS")
scenarios: The SHA-first checkout fails or lands on github.sha; the refspec-based fetch that would have correctly resolved the patchset is downstream and cannot substitute for it

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (or make explicit in the plan) that the exact-SHA checkout reaches the revision via a fetched refs/changes/* ref rather than assuming actions/checkout can resolve a bare unadvertised commit SHA from the mirror.
evidence: Plan step 1: 'check out ref: ${{ inputs.GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION }} with fetch-depth: 1'
GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION is a raw commit SHA (workflow input description: 'Gerrit patchset revision (commit SHA)'), not a branch/tag; on the mirror it is only reachable via a refs/changes/* ref.
No plan text establishes that actions/checkout resolves a bare unadvertised revision SHA against origin (as opposed to a branch/tag/PR-number ref it fetches by name).
findings.finding: The plan assumes actions/checkout can check out a bare commit SHA (GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION) that is not a branch/tag/PR ref, but does not establish that actions/checkout will fetch an unadvertised revision object from the mirror; actions/checkout fetches the given ref and a bare arbitrary SHA is only obtainable if reachable from a fetched ref.
findings.location: Fix plan, step 1; Acceptance Criteria AC1
scenarios: Even without replication lag, actions/checkout given a bare revision SHA (rather than the refs/changes/* refspec that advertises it) may fail to locate the object unless the SHA happens to be the tip of a fetched ref.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify replacing the repo-standard checkout-gerrit-change-action with hand-rolled plumbing in this lane vs. the narrower alternative (validate the GERRIT_REFSPEC<->GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION pair while keeping the pinned action), and reconcile the divergence with ADR-0021.
evidence: The action lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action is the standard across gerrit-verify.yaml, _build-and-test.yml, _mutation.yml, _optionality.yml, _eval-discipline.yml, _artifact-probe.yml
Plan: 'delegates the final checkout to a refspec-first third-party action even though this lane's authoritative requested commit is GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION'
A narrower fix (validate refspec<->GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION pair, or assert FETCH_HEAD, while KEEPING the pinned action) is the established alternative and is not weighed in the plan
ADR-0021 accepts the mirror-first/Gerrit-fallback checkout via this action as the architectural decision
findings.finding: The plan replaces the repo-standard third-party Gerrit checkout action with a novel hand-rolled actions/checkout + shell-fetch pattern for this one lane, without justifying the novelty against the established repo-wide approach or against the narrower alternative of validating the refspec/revision pair while keeping the existing action.
scenarios: Reviewers/maintainers must reconcile one lane using a bespoke checkout while every other Gerrit lane uses the shared action
A future Gerrit-checkout behavior change (e.g., ADR-0021 mirror semantics) updates the shared action but silently bypasses this lane

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the capability assumption that actions/checkout with ref=<full patchset SHA> reliably checks out an unmerged Gerrit patchset (mirror-lag case) and leaves an authenticated origin remote able to fetch arbitrary refs/changes/* refspecs, or fetch by explicit URL per the _build-and-test.yml precedent.
evidence: Plan: 'It fetches from the existing origin remote created by actions/checkout (the GitHub mirror, with the workflow token/auth setup already handled by actions/checkout)'
_build-and-test.yml lines 547-554 fetch main's tip 'by EXPLICIT URL from the canonical GitHub repo' precisely 'so the lock does NOT depend on an origin remote being configured by the checkout action'

The plan does not confirm that actions/checkout with ref=<full SHA> and fetch-depth:1 leaves an origin remote whose auth can fetch an arbitrary refs/changes/* refspec, nor whether a full-SHA ref checkout can even resolve without the refspec being fetched first
findings.finding: The plan's step-2 fetch relies on 'the existing origin remote created by actions/checkout (... with the workflow token/auth setup already handled by actions/checkout)' — an unverified capability assertion that differs from the repo's own established explicit-URL fetch precedent, which was written because a Gerrit checkout does not guarantee an origin remote.
scenarios: A patchset SHA not yet replicated to the GitHub mirror: actions/checkout with ref=<SHA> may fail to check out before step 2's fallback ever runs
origin fetch of refs/changes/NN/NNNN/P via the actions/checkout token succeeds/fails differently than assumed, silently falling through to (or failing) the HTTPS fallback

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (or SPIKE) that `actions/checkout` with `ref:` set to a bare Gerrit patchset commit SHA actually resolves against the GitHub mirror `origin`; if it cannot fetch an arbitrary SHA, invert the order (fetch `GERRIT_REFSPEC` first, then check out `FETCH_HEAD`/the verified SHA) rather than relying on SHA-first checkout.
evidence: Every other lane checks out patchsets via lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action with an explicit gerrit-refspec `refs/changes/NN/NNNN/P` (gerrit-verify.yaml lines 71-75, 127-131, 170-174, 299-303, 353-358; _build-and-test.yml; _mutation.yml) — not by bare SHA

gerrit-verify.yaml classify job (lines 132-139) must run a `git fetch --deepen` loop after the Gerrit checkout to make the patchset parent diffable, evidence that patchset-commit reachability on the mirror is not guaranteed

Evidence class: Partially-verified — actions/checkout exists and is used repo-wide, but the specific surface (ref:=arbitrary Gerrit patchset SHA on the mirror) is unconfirmed and contradicted by existing usage patterns
findings.finding: The plan's step 1 assumes `actions/checkout` with `ref: ${{ inputs.GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION }}` can check out an arbitrary Gerrit patchset commit SHA against the GitHub mirror, but this external capability is unverified and likely does not hold: actions/checkout resolves branches/tags/PR-refs, and a bare commit SHA is only fetchable when the server advertises a reachable ref for it. A Gerrit patchset commit lives under refs/changes/* on Gerrit and need not be present on the GitHub mirror at all.
findings.location: Fix plan step 1 ("Use the already-approved, SHA-pinned `actions/checkout` action to check out `ref: ${{ inputs.GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION }}` with `fetch-depth: 1`")
scenarios: A patchset whose commit is not present on the GitHub mirror (fresh patchset, mirror sync lag) is dispatched; step 1's actions/checkout fails to resolve the SHA and the job aborts before the refspec fetch/fallback in step 2 ever runs
findings.suggested_fix: Fetch the refspec first (git fetch origin/anonymous-HTTPS ${GERRIT_REFSPEC}), assert FETCH_HEAD^{commit} == GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION, then `git checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD` — this both lands the exact patchset and validates it, without depending on actions/checkout resolving a bare Gerrit SHA.
